edit.description: set it at the invoke site the verdict row's tag is set from
what the invocation carries under each concurrency

summary: Report the provisioned entry's tag on `AgentInvocation`, so a decorator reads it instead of regexing the rendered prompt

per.section: A fact the engine holds is reported, never rediscovered

tests: a fanout agent invocation carries the provisioned entry's tag
pins: a singleton agent invocation carries no entry tag
acceptance: The invocation carries the tag under fanout and carries none under singleton, the same rule `TickVerdictInvocation.tag` already follows; tsc and vitest green.
notes: Survey: a metrics decorator recovers the tag by regexing `opts.prompt`, because the tag is first-class on `TickContext.assignedEntry` and unreachable from a decorator composed in a phase getter (consumer-b.md §3 #4). `invokeAgent` already takes `ref.key`; the fanout call site has `entry.tag` in scope.

what a teardown reaper reads instead of the directory

summary: Hand chains git's worktree registry on `FlumeApi`, so a teardown reaper reads the engine's list instead of walking `.flume/worktrees/`
tests: FlumeApi reports the worktrees git registers for the repo
an unreadable worktree registry reports the failure rather than an empty set
acceptance: A chain can answer "which worktrees does git still register" off the API, absence and unreadability distinguishable; tsc and vitest green.
notes: `readWorktreeRegistry` (`src/worktrees.ts:119`) is module-private and already returns the loud union — `{ read: false, reason }` never collapses into an empty set. Survey: a consumer allocates a DB per fanout arm and reaps orphans by enumerating `.flume/worktrees/`, the only instance of a chain reading an engine-owned directory (consumer-d.md §3 #4, §7).
